title: Why the AGM converges doubly exponentially
content: The arithmetic–geometric mean iteration $a_{n+1} = (a_n+b_n)/2$, $b_{n+1} = \sqrt{a_n b_n}$ is famous for converging *quadratically*: the gap $a_n - b_n$ contracts doubly exponentially, not merely geometrically. This file isolates the mechanism in two independent halves — a per-step algebraic identity showing each step squares the gap, and an abstract recursion lemma turning $g_{n+1} \le g_n^2/C$ into the $(\cdot)^{2^n}$ rate. Both are proved with 0 axioms; the second half is geometry-free and applies to any quadratically convergent process (e.g. Newton's method).

title: Each AGM step squares the gap
content: `agm_gap_eq` proves the one-step identity $(a+b)/2 - \sqrt{ab} = (\sqrt a - \sqrt b)^2/2$ — the gap after a step is half the square of the difference of square roots (expand $\sqrt{ab} = \sqrt a\,\sqrt b$ and $(\sqrt a)^2 = a$, then `nlinarith`). `agm_gap_quadratic` then factors $(\sqrt a - \sqrt b)(\sqrt a + \sqrt b) = a - b$ to rewrite it as $(a-b)^2/(2(\sqrt a + \sqrt b)^2)$, exhibiting the new gap as proportional to the *square* of the old gap. Squaring the error each step is precisely what quadratic convergence means.

title: A clean recursion gₙ₊₁ ≤ gₙ²/(8b)
content: `agm_gap_le` bounds the step by $(a-b)^2/(8b)$ for $0 < b \le a$. Since $\sqrt a \ge \sqrt b$, we have $(\sqrt a + \sqrt b)^2 \ge (2\sqrt b)^2 = 4b$, hence $2(\sqrt a + \sqrt b)^2 \ge 8b$ and the quadratic form is at most $(a-b)^2/(8b)$ (closed by `gcongr` after the denominator bound). This packages the squaring into a recursion $g_{n+1} \le g_n^2/(8b)$ whose denominator is controlled by the *smaller* term — exactly the shape the abstract iteration lemma consumes.

title: Recursion to rate: the doubly exponential bound
content: `quadratic_iteration` is the geometry-free engine: any nonnegative sequence with $g_{n+1} \le g_n^2/C$ (for $C>0$) satisfies $g_n \le C\,(g_0/C)^{2^n}$. The induction squares the inductive bound and uses $2^{n+1} = 2^n\cdot 2$ (`pow_succ`, `pow_mul`) to land on the next exponent; the base case is $g_0 = C(g_0/C)^1$. This is the doubly exponential rate the problem asks for — the gap raised to the $2^n$ power, far faster than any geometric decay — and the same lemma governs Newton's method and other quadratically convergent iterations.

title: Separating the geometry from the rate
content: A structural highlight: the proof cleanly splits the analytic content (the AGM-specific gap identity and squaring bound) from the combinatorial content (the abstract $g_{n+1} \le g_n^2/C \Rightarrow g_n \le C(g_0/C)^{2^n}$ recursion). `quadratic_iteration` mentions no square roots and no AGM at all — it is a reusable statement about *any* quadratically contracting sequence. Composing it with `agm_gap_le` yields the AGM rate, but the same lemma instantly transfers to Newton's method, Halley's method, or any other process whose error squares each step.
mathContext: Reusable: $g_{n+1} \le g_n^2/C$ governs every quadratically convergent iteration.
